newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Biotech firm to boost investments in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Biotech firm to boost investments in Asia.

text.p: A life science venture capital company managing more than US$100 million in assets will use Singapore as a hub for regional investment, Arthur Pappas, founder of A.M. Pappas & Associates (AMP&A), said on Wednesday.

"With Singapore as a hub for life science research and development in Asia, our regional office expects to invest about half of the US$100 million in the next several years directly in promising technologies, products and companies here and in the region," said Pappas, who also is chief executive officer.
He said Singapore has the best bio-medical infrastructure in the region with a market valued at an estimated US$2.5 billion.
The U.S.-based management and consulting company targets small to medium-sized companies.
Scientists and small companies can reduce the time it takes to develop and market technologies through its venture process, which provides fully integrated support.
It typically takes about 10 to 15 years to develop, test and market a product, but this time could be reduced to seven to 10 years, Pappas told a news conference.
The company's venture development model gets around inefficiencies in traditional funding and development by offering a range of scientific and commercial expertise, officials said.

"AMP&A's distinction from other venture capital companies is its prominent scientific and technical aspect to its venture capital process," said AMP&A's C. Victor Shi, director of operations Asia and general manager for Singapore. Shi said AMP&A was working closely with the National Science and Technology Board and the National University of Singapore to help the university develop commercial uses for technologies emerging from its medical research.
AMP&A has identified three projects to be based in Singapore for the near-term and expects one company to start by mid-year.
It is also helping companies enter markets in Taiwan, China, Malaysia and Indonesia.
